To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypothalamic preprongrowth hormone-releasing hormone (GRF) messenger (m)RNA is decreased in 72-h fasted rats and restored to fed levels by refeeding diets containing 8-12% protein.
dietary protein regulates the expression of hypothalamic preprorGH-RF mRNA and that dietary fat has no effect on hypothalamic prepropGH-RF mRNA.
dietary protein deprivation is sufficient to decrease hypothalamic pre-proGRF mRNA in the rat and that the decrease is reversed by feeding a protein-containing diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which dietary protein and amino acids regulate growth hormone (GH) synthesis and secretion and the role of GH as a mediator of the anabolic effects of dietary protein.
the role of dietary protein and amino acids in the regulation of the GH/IGF-1 axis.
the regulation of the synthesis and secretion of the hypothalamic peptide growth hormone-releasing factor (GRF), which is an important stimulant for growth hormone secretion from the pituitary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary protein regulates hypothalamic preprongrowth hormone-releasing hormone messenger ribonuclei acid expression.
the GRF response in rats to food deprivation is due to a lack of dietary protein.
hypothalamic prepropGRF mRNA is regulated by the amount of protein in the diet, not the total caloric intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary protein is required for normal growth hormone secretion.
the hypothalamic GRF response to nutrient restriction is mediated via the action of dietary protein.

dietary protein is required for the maintenance of normal hypothalamic pre-proGRF mRNA and that dietary protein deprivation is sufficient to decrease hypothalamic prepropGH mRNA expression in adult rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein is the most potent nutrient for the regulation of preproGRF synthesis.
the hypothalamic GRF system is regulated by dietary protein and that GRF may play an important role in the anabolic effects of protein.
the regulation of preproGRF gene expression by protein in the diet appears to be mediated by the availability of dietary amino acids, rather than by caloric restriction.
